content: If we had no weaknesses, we should not take so much pleasure in observing those of other men.
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
sourceWork: Memoirs of the Regency of Anne of Austria
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. We spend enormous energy trying to present a sanitized, perfect version of ourselves to the world. But whatever emotions or desires we push into the dark don't disappear; they run our lives from behind the curtain.

François de La Rochefoucauld understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. True maturity isn't pretending you have no dark corners—it is having the honesty and courage to look at your jealousy, fear, and anger in the daylight so they no longer control your actions.
reflectionPrompt: What hidden motive, insecurity, or fear might be silently driving your recent reactions?
